newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian president resumes some official duties.
newsitem.headline: Austrian president resumes some official duties.

text.p: Ailing Austrian President Thomas Klestil resumed limited official duties on Friday but Chancellor Franz Vranitzky said he would remain in hospital for some time.
The chancellor, who took over as acting head of state on September 23, had earlier paid Klestil a brief visit in Vienna General Hospital, where he is recovering from acute pneumonia.
"I have told the president that I will no longer represent him given the improvement in his health," Vranitzky told Austrian radio.
It was the two men's first meeting since Klestil's admission to hospital on September 13 and his transfer to intensive care one week later.
Vranitzky said the 63-year-old president was now able to shoulder a light workload but had cancelled all trips abroad.
"The doctors say he is well on the way to recovery but due to the severity of his illness it will be some time -- possibly one to two weeks -- before he can go home," Vranitzky said.

Official secrecy over Klestil's condition angered some Austrian politicians, including Vranitzky who was annoyed that doctors failed to alert government leaders immediately when Klestil fell into unconsciousness two weeks ago.
Vranitzky said he was determined to clarify procedures for releasing information in future cases of presidential illness.
"I have undertaken to improve lines of communication and I believe I can achieve that quite easily," the chancellor said.
He criticised media handling of the incident, however, and insisted even public figures had a right to privacy.

The president's office has spent much of the past two weeks denying newspaper reports that Klestil is suffering from AIDS or cancer. Political commentators noted that official secrecy only served to fuel the more fanciful reports.
Klestil's resumption of limited duties appeared to quash speculation that he may have to step down, which would mean a presidential election two years ahead of schedule.

Klestil became president in 1992 and helped restore Austria's image abroad after his predecessor Kurt Waldheim's controversial period of office. Waldheim was shunned by most foreign leaders for concealing his Nazi past.
